Healthcare fraud costs Americans billions. Look at the ACA numbers: $11B lost to improper enrollments under loose verification standards. That's not speculation—that's documented waste hitting taxpayer wallets.

Tightening enrollment periods isn't about denying care—it's about protecting the system's integrity. When bureaucrats rubber-stamp applications without proper checks, legitimate recipients suffer while funds vanish into fraudulent claims.

The solution is straightforward: verify eligibility upfront, track every federal dollar, and prosecute abuse. No exceptions, no special carve-outs. Rep. Hoyer can spin this as "restricting access," but real access depends on a solvent, fraud-free system.

Accountability in healthcare isn't partisan—it's essential. For millions of families counting on these programs, every dollar lost to fraud is care denied to someone who truly needs it.

Medicaid’s real problem isn’t funding—it’s bureaucratic bloat. HHS spending ballooned from $1.2T to $1.7T in 5 years, yet hospitals still price-gouge patients while administrators pocket taxpayer cash. Cutting waste means redirecting funds to actual care, not slashing coverage.

The GOP plan misses the point: Target fraud, not families. D.C. burns billions on overpriced contracts and middlemen while patients suffer.

Fix the system, don’t just trim the budget.

The real scandal? Medicaid’s $172B in improper payments last year alone. CBO’s math misses the point—Washington’s addiction to bloated bureaucracy is the disease, not the cure.

The Department of Government Efficiency clawed back $32B in canceled contracts this year by targeting waste, not coverage. If bureaucrats stopped funneling cash to failed programs and overpriced vendors, we’d have plenty to fund care without bankrupting taxpayers.

Reform starts with audits, not austerity theater.

Sadly, Republicans remain focused on forcing through their "big, beautiful bill" that rips health care coverage away from millions of Americans and explodes the national debt in order to pass their massive tax cuts for the wealthiest individuals.

The real issue? Medicaid is collapsing under bureaucratic bloat AND unchecked illegal immigration draining resources. The CBO projects 10.9 million losing coverage because the system prioritizes waste over taxpayers.

Nursing homes struggle not from funding cuts but from states diverting $162 billion to loopholes benefiting non-citizens. Every dollar spent on ER mandates for those who broke immigration laws steals care from seniors who paid into the system.

Fix the structural rot, not the budget.

The "Republican attack" on Medicaid isn't some abstract fight; it's the direct consequence of the Trump admin's relentless pursuit of tax cuts for billionaire donors, funded by gutting healthcare for millions. Maryland alone faces a $1 billion blow, a stark reminder that the admin's promises to protect entitlements are routinely sacrificed for its self-serving agenda.

This isn't a carefully reviewed plan by experts, but a chaotic raid on vital programs, echoing the 2020 budget's proposed $1.5 trillion Medicaid slash and the 2025 "One Big Beautiful Bill" that again targeted Medicaid for trillions in cuts. While the admin claims fiscal responsibility, these cuts will kick Marylanders off health insurance and force hospitals nationwide to abandon critical services, all to pad the pockets of the wealthy. This systemic dismantling of the social safety net, enabled by Republican allies, reveals an admin that prioritizes its interests over the health and well-being of every American.

The American people deserve accountability for an admin that consistently trades their healthcare for donor handouts.

Democrats scream "crisis" while pushing the same failed policies that created this mess. The Protecting Health Care and Lowering Costs Act of 2025 exposes their scam: expanding subsidies without fixing systemic fraud. Medicare loses $60B annually to billing scams while Big Pharma jacks up drug prices through patent abuse.

Republicans rightly demand accountability - why pour billions into ACA marketplaces when 1 in 5 Medicaid enrollees aren’t even eligible? The shutdown persists because Democrats prioritize expanding coverage loopholes over cutting waste.

Real reform means auditing hospital billing, breaking pharma monopolies, and stopping the $150B annual hemorrhage in healthcare fraud - not doubling down on bloated subsidies.

The real crisis isn’t partisan gridlock—it’s a healthcare system rigged by Big Pharma monopolies and bureaucratic bloat. While DC plays blame games, families face $1,900 premium spikes because Washington refuses to cut middlemen profiting off overpriced drugs and hospital price-gouging.

The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1) proves real reform is possible: redirecting $1.6T from globalist handouts to patient-first care. But career politicians protect their donor class instead.

Want cheaper healthcare? Crush the cartels inflating costs, not taxpayers.

Hoyer’s panic ignores reality. The ACA’s premium spikes aren’t Trump’s fault—they’re baked into Obamacare’s broken model. The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R.1) slashes $1.6T in waste, redirecting funds from bloated bureaucracies to empower patients.

Democrats scream “costs” while sneaking benefits for illegals into every bill. The real issue? Big Pharma’s grip on D.C. inflates prices, and ACA subsidies are a band-aid on a hemorrhage.

Check your plan—but know the root problem is government-run healthcare, not Trump’s fiscal discipline. Time to dismantle the scam, not prop it up.
